_about: The lifespans lane. From Adam to Joseph the dates are counted from the text: each person's `fatherAge` is how old their father was at their birth (Genesis 5, 11:10-26, 21:5, 25:26, and Joseph from 41:46-47 with 45:6 and 47:9), and the build works them out from Abram's birth in 2166 BC (`anchor`). Shem is born when Noah is 502, since Shem was 100 two years after the Flood (11:10). Abram is counted as born when Terah was 130 (Acts 7:4 with Genesis 11:32 and 12:4). Moses, Aaron and Joshua are dated from the Exodus in 1446. After them a life is given as `born`/`died`: the kings of Judah from their age at accession (on Thiele's dates, as in kings.json), David from 2 Samuel 5:4, Eli from 1 Samuel 4:15, Ezekiel from 'the thirtieth year' (Ezekiel 1:1), and the rest from the events around them, marked `approx` where the text gives no age.

lives.name: Enoch
lives.note: Walked with God, and was not, for God took him.

lives.name: Methuselah
lives.note: The longest life in Scripture; he died in the year of the Flood.

lives.name: Peleg
lives.note: In his days the earth was divided.

lives.name: Aaron
lives.note: Three years older than Moses; died on Mount Hor at 123, in the fortieth year after the Exodus.

lives.name: Moses
lives.note: Forty years in Pharaoh's court, forty in Midian, forty leading Israel.

lives.name: Joshua
lives.note: His birth is not given; he died at 110, after the land had rest.

lives.name: Sarah
lives.note: Ten years younger than Abraham; she bore Isaac at ninety and died at 127.

lives.name: Ishmael
lives.note: Abraham's son by Hagar, born when Abraham was eighty-six.

lives.name: Miriam
lives.note: Moses' older sister, who watched over him in the Nile; she died at Kadesh in the last year of the wilderness.

lives.name: Caleb
lives.note: Forty when he spied out the land, and still as strong at eighty-five when he took Hebron. His death is not given.

lives.name: Eli
lives.note: Priest at Shiloh; he died at ninety-eight on hearing that the ark was taken.

lives.name: Samson
lives.note: A Nazirite from birth; he judged Israel twenty years and died bringing down the temple of Dagon.

lives.name: Samuel
lives.note: Born in answer to Hannah's prayer; he died before Saul did, mourned by all Israel.

lives.name: Saul
lives.note: About thirty when he became king, by the usual reading of 1 Samuel 13:1.

lives.name: Jonathan
lives.note: Saul's son and David's friend; he fell with his father on Mount Gilboa.

lives.name: David
lives.note: Thirty when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

lives.name: Solomon
lives.note: Young when he was crowned; his son Rehoboam was already born a year before.

lives.name: Joash
lives.note: Hidden in the Temple as a baby and crowned at seven.

lives.name: Uzziah
lives.note: King at sixteen; he died a leper, the year Isaiah saw the Lord.

lives.name: Hezekiah
lives.note: King at twenty-five; given fifteen more years when he was dying.

lives.name: Manasseh
lives.note: King at twelve, the longest reign in Judah.

lives.name: Josiah
lives.note: King at eight; he sought God at sixteen and died at thirty-nine.

lives.name: Jeremiah
lives.note: Called as 'only a youth' in 627; last heard of in Egypt.

lives.name: Jehoiachin
lives.note: King at eighteen for three months, then thirty-seven years a prisoner in Babylon before he was released.

lives.name: Ezekiel
lives.note: Thirty when his visions began in 593; the last is dated 571.

lives.name: Daniel
lives.note: Taken to Babylon as a young man in 605, still there in the third year of Cyrus.

lives.name: John the Baptist
lives.note: Six months older than Jesus; beheaded by Herod Antipas.

lives.name: Jesus
lives.note: Born before Herod died in 4 BC, about thirty when his ministry began (Luke 3:23), crucified and risen in AD 30.

lives.name: Peter
lives.note: A Galilean fisherman; martyred at Rome under Nero, by early tradition.

lives.name: Paul
lives.note: 'A young man' at Stephen's stoning, 'Paul the aged' by Philemon; beheaded at Rome, by early tradition.

lives.name: John
lives.note: The youngest of the apostles by tradition, and the last to die, at Ephesus around AD 100.
